dimensions.note: Owner verdict (human, Linear SUE-570 §D): infographic composition is a material failure. The mechanism, read from source: four modules at hand-assigned coordinates in a 2x2 arrangement whose axes encode nothing. It borrows the appearance of a matrix without the encoding, which is worse than no grid because it implies a comparison that does not exist. The modules are lettered A/B/C/D precisely because the geometry cannot say what the order is.
dimensions.evidence: SVG source read 2026-09-06: modules at (24,50), (368,50), (24,200), (368,200). Failure signature F1.

dimensions.note: Twelve drawn enclosures for four load-bearing modules — cards containing chips containing text. Failure signature F2.
dimensions.evidence: 13 rect elements including background; 4 module cards, 7 chips/accent bars, 1 dashed conclusion box.

dimensions.note: Semantically dense in element count but not in relationships: two of four modules contain no geometry at all, only prose inside a rectangle, so the first-read payload equals the sentences the plate was derived from. Failure signature F3.
dimensions.evidence: Modules C and D consist solely of text elements inside a bordered rect.

dimensions.note: One plate answering four primary questions plus a fifth it explicitly declines to answer. Failure signature F4.
dimensions.evidence: In-frame question is about whether the spreadsheet path applies to AI; modules answer mechanism, authority shift, flat-vs-centralized, and where the analogy breaks.

dimensions.note: 22 text elements against the profile's stated label_count_ceiling of 8, and the article title plus publication date baked into the artwork where the caption layer should own them. Failure signatures F6 and F7.
dimensions.evidence: visual-body-infographic.json text_policy.label_count_ceiling is 8; nothing in the producing path checked it.

dimensions.note: Fixed viewBox with no breakpoint, so the only response to a narrow viewport is uniform scaling: module labels render at roughly 5.7px and notes at 5.2px on a ~358px figure width. Failure signature F5.
dimensions.evidence: 720px intrinsic width against suengj.com --width-article of 42rem; scale 0.497 at a ~390px viewport.

dimensions.note: Retained as negative evidence for visual/body-infographic. It is citable as a failure and must never be selected as generation evidence.

weaknesses: Spatial position encodes no relation; the layout could be permuted without changing what the plate asserts.
More drawn containers than load-bearing modules.
Half the plate is prose inside rectangles.
Fails the ~390px mobile gate by roughly a factor of two, with no mobile strategy attempted.
Mutable article title and date baked into artwork.
notes: NEGATIVE evidence. Basis corrected 2026-09-06 after independent review: the owner's explicit judgement (Linear SUE-570 §D) is that infographic composition is a material failure, and that verdict is human. The per-dimension verdicts below — spacing, hierarchy, visual-density, label-text-strategy — are this agent's reading of the SVG source, not things the owner said, so the record's basis is model_inference and claiming explicit_human_feedback for all of them overstated it. Deliberately carries no promotion block: a generated_output reference without promotion is excluded from the positive selection path, which is the mechanism that keeps SUE-570 output from becoming a GOOD reference.
